title: Canonical coefficient actions on scalar-localized derived module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal S$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $A$ a commutative ring, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $a:A\to\Gamma(\mathcal S,R)$ a ring homomorphism. Use the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and its global-section action on morphisms [def-pur-sheaf-modules-hom-module]. The canonical $A$-linear structure on $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is obtained by restricting that global-section action along $a$ and then using the induced linear structure on the localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms. For $t\in A$, put $R_t=R[1/t]$ by sheafified section localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization] and let $A[1/t]$ be the coefficient ring localization [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Define $a_t:A[1/t]\to\Gamma(\mathcal S,R_t)$ as the unique localization lift of the composite $A\xrightarrow a\Gamma(\mathcal S,R)\to\Gamma(\mathcal S,R_t)$, sending $t^{-1}$ to the inverse of the localized section $a(t)$. The canonical $A[1/t]$-linear structure on $D(R_t)$ is the same induced construction applied to $(A[1/t],R_t,a_t)$. These are the specified scalar actions, including when $t=0$, $t$ is nilpotent, or $R$ is the zero ring; no action is chosen arbitrarily.
